claim: Observed same-server phase-switch savings with identical output and final resource drain; bounded C1 workloads only.
limitations: Two timing processes per arm/profile in ABBA order, 16 measured requests per process. No confidence interval or statistical-significance claim.

B1/C1, requested four-token random input and 8 or 64 output tokens; the client records three-token input lengths after tokenization. Long prefill, multi-request batching, sustained load and other devices remain unqualified.
The short-output P99 TPOT increases about 16.8%. A first decode interval is 287 ms in one capacity-two run and 137 ms in the other; those initial requests are included, not discarded.
Median steady inter-token latency remains about 23.6 ms. The measured improvement comes from avoiding full graph reconstruction across phases, not a demonstrated faster generated kernel.

Both arms use the same verified executable, artifact, tuning and provider sources. The serving artifact is newly selected for its own state-pool geometry and cannot be compared with the earlier executor artifact as a kernel speedup.
Shared FP8 quantization is explicitly enabled by the common tuning profile for this experiment; its production default and graph-cache capacity default are unchanged.

The independent HTTP oracle checks three generated tokens. Full random-trace text matches exactly across all four runs per profile. Prior full-logit regression records use their own artifacts; this record does not claim an independent full-logit oracle for every HTTP token.
Existing OS/provider caches are retained. Startup, provider setup and compilation are excluded from serving metrics. Timings contain no stage tracing or per-node CUDA profile events.
Final resource census verifies request/KV/fixed-state drain; CUDA driver allocation peak is not measured. Provider memory budgeting remains conservative and residency selection is manual.

Active-stream termination takes about 10.5 seconds including the frontend graceful-shutdown interval. It cancels the outstanding request and releases state; it is not an immediate-shutdown latency result.
